Zcash has set a new high in its network hashrate just days after the NU7 upgrade, which slashed block times by a third to 25 seconds. Zcash activated its NU7 upgrade on November 6, 2026, at block 3,543,405.

Zcash network hashrate: 32.62 GSol/s, up 5.8% in 30 days. ⛏️ An all-time high. https://t.co/1vNROBAvd2

Zcash hashrate refers to the total computing power of all miners on the ZEC network. It is calculated by the current network difficulty, the average block find time set by the cryptocurrency network and/or the effective block find time of the latest blocks.

ZEC got 3x faster following the NU7 upgrade, which launched on November 6, with block times down from 75 to 25 seconds, and the Sprout pool retired, marking a new era for Zcash.

Faster blocks mean more room for shielded transactions. NU7 adds per-block limits: 330 Orchard or Ironwood actions, 300 Sapling inputs and outputs, a shared budget of 330 across pools, and no new Sprout JoinSplits. These limits more than double Orchard protocol throughput while reducing the worst-case sync load a spammer can push onto light wallets by about 37%.

NU7 does not raise Zcash's fixed 21 million cap; halvings will now come every 5,040,000 blocks instead of 1,680,000, so the issuance schedule holds at roughly four years per halving. NU7 also starts allocating funds for future mining rewards. Some 60% of aggregate transaction fees will flow into a public reserve that pays later mining rewards.

In what comes next after the NU7 upgrade, Zcash developers have proposed cutting block times in a potential NU7.1 upgrade just days after NU7 went live. The proposal would reduce target block times from 25 to 20 seconds, aiming to speed up transaction confirmations and improve user experience and network latency.

TL;DR: A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology.

A tokenized share transaction involving a Nasdaq-listed company has taken place on Canton under a US regulatory exemption, according to an announcement from venue operator TSV. The November 4 transaction involved shares of Canton Strategic Holdings and a permissioned pool using Tradecraft's automated market maker technology. The important development is not that a stock price was mirrored on a blockchain, but that the transaction was structured around the issuer, a transfer agent and verified holders.

TSV says DRW Cumberland purchased tokenized Canton Strategic Holdings common stock from existing shareholder Five North. Fairmint, an SEC-registered transfer agent, recorded the shares in token form in a verified wallet, and Flowdesk provided liquidity. The parties describe this as the first trade of its kind under the SEC's innovation exemption. Because this is an operator announcement, the scope of that first-of-kind claim should be attributed to the participants. What can be identified concretely is the named issuer, the parties, the permissioned environment and the transfer-agent role in the share record.

Tokenized equities can describe several very different products. Some are economic exposures issued by a separate intermediary; others aim to represent the issuer's shares with the rights and recordkeeping attached to conventional stock. Here the issuer-sponsored structure and transfer-agent involvement are central. They are intended to connect token holdings with the legally recognized ownership register, rather than just a derivative tracking a market price. Investors still need to know transfer restrictions, voting rights, eligibility rules and how corporate actions are administered. A blockchain token is not proof of all those protections by itself.

The reported transactions occurred in a permissioned pool with verified participants. That is fundamentally different from announcing that any wallet can buy US shares without checks or through a decentralized exchange. Restricted access may be a design choice needed to satisfy securities obligations, investor eligibility and transfer controls. It may also limit liquidity and interoperability compared with the open token markets crypto users are accustomed to. The test of such infrastructure is whether these controls can function at scale without making trading and settlement more cumbersome than conventional systems.

The company referred to an SEC innovation exemption announced in September. The transaction should be read within the specific conditions of the applicable relief, not as proof the SEC has deregulated all tokenized securities. Different venues, issuers or instruments may require their own legal analysis. Reporting on this area is especially sensitive to the distinction between an operational pilot, a live limited transaction and a broadly available retail market. This appears to be the second category: a real transaction, but with explicit participation boundaries.

Future announcements should reveal the number and variety of issuers, whether transactions settle consistently, how ownership and voting are handled, and whether participants can transfer positions between approved venues. Costs, order-book depth and operational incidents will be more revealing than another first-trade headline. If tokenized US equities become a durable market structure, those unglamorous details will matter at least as much as the chain carrying the record.

#5199. “I’ll Block for This”: Ripple’s Schwartz Sets Reply Rules

Home » Ripple (XRP) » “I’ll Block for This”: Ripple’s Schwartz Sets Reply Rules

The move follows a rise in negative XRP commentary that has little to do with the actual threads.

David Schwartz, known on X as JoelKatz and one of the original architects of the XRP Ledger, has begun blocking accounts that insert crypto-related comments or accusations into his non-crypto conversations.

Schwartz explained that a growing number of people are responding to his replies on unrelated topics with crypto content or insults. When that happens, the people he is talking to end up with their followers seeing the off-topic posts.

He described the pattern as forcing those users into a choice: either tolerate the spam or block him. To avoid that outcome, he has started blocking the accounts responsible.

A significant share of the posts, he noted, accuse him of fraud or scamming. He stated he will block this behavior regardless of whether the comment is framed as XRP criticism or praise.

Schwartz drew a distinction between relevant criticism and irrelevant spam. He wrote that he does not mind people criticizing him or accusing him of wrongdoing, provided the posts contain actual content and avoid simple slurs.

Recently, there's been a significant increase in people responding to replies of mine that have nothing to do with crypto with insults or crypto content. I hate to do it, but I pretty much have to block for this because otherwise the people I'm replying to have no choice but to…

The condition is placement: such comments should appear in the critic’s own threads or in replies to his posts where the topic has at least some relevance.

What he said he will not tolerate is users following him across X specifically to insert “scammer” or even positive XRP comments into conversations that have nothing to do with crypto. Those replies, he argued, anger the people whose threads are being used.

For anyone already blocked under this policy, Schwartz left an opening. He said that if the person promises not to repeat the behavior and finds a way to get his attention, he will unblock them.

The offer stands even if the user continues to strongly dislike him. The stated limit is simple: do not use his replies to spam other people’s followers.

Some replies eagerly pushed back, arguing that frustration with Ripple’s performance or past expectations justified the critical comments. Others framed the blocks as an attempt to avoid accountability.

Can I honestly say that I have nothing to do with the price of XRP? I guess probably not nothing. But very little. pic.twitter.com/8Plpyw61IZ

Schwartz’s post itself focused on the practical problem of irrelevant replies landing in other users’ timelines rather than on any broader debate about XRP or Ripple.

The new policy amounts to a clear boundary on where and how he is willing to engage on the platform. Criticism remains acceptable in relevant spaces. Off-topic insertions into unrelated conversations, whether hostile or not, are now grounds for a block.

#5197. Ethereum (ETH) Gas Estimates Are Broken: Explaining the Fix and the Issue

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Ethereum transactions can appear successful, but there might be a problem hiding behind the scenes.

A Geth developer has proposed a fix to the client's gas estimation, according to draft pull request #36084 on GitHub. The patch addresses an issue in the current estimator, which could result in incorrect gas limits due to failed internal calls (calls from one smart contract to another) being ignored.

Although the transaction could still be completed, there is no evidence that the action the user wanted has actually happened.

The issue lies in a mechanism where a smart contract calls another smart contract, catches an error, and then proceeds to a refund, records the failure, or skips an item entirely. Technically, the transaction was successful, but the outcome is different for the user.

This could potentially result in wallets suggesting a gas limit that is enough to finish the transaction, but not enough to complete the work inside it. The developer also noted that EIP-8037 could make this behavior more common, since gas returned from failed internal execution can help fund the fallback.

According to the pull request, the change includes a stricter definition of success for gas estimates. This version of Geth would improve the way it deals with internal failures, counting failed internal calls and contract creations instead of checking only whether the transaction completes.

Even if the transaction completes, the estimate would get rejected if it produces more internal failures than a reference execution with a higher gas limit.

Nonetheless, the developer stressed that an internal call that always fails should not push the estimate higher indefinitely. The reference execution enables the estimator to keep existing failures without allowing additional ones caused by insufficient gas. The proposal also introduces a separate Amsterdam reference, preventing unnecessary increases made purely to access the state gas reservoir.

The developer states that they've replayed 432 mainnet transactions with the new set of rules from the Amsterdam update and that the suggested change fixed 64 out of 67 cases.

The gas limit increased by 4%. 254 additional estimates were unaffected due to the lack of the problem, with 3 cases being undetected.

For regular investors, the proposed change should improve the reliability of wallet estimates and reduce transactions that complete without delivering the intended result, despite introducing higher gas limits in some cases. Luckily, there is no proven link between higher gas limits and higher fees.

#5196. Broadridge Says Blockchain Repo Platform Processed $7.6T in October

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens.

Broadridge says its Distributed Ledger Repo service processed $7.6 trillion in repurchase agreement transactions during October, averaging $345 billion a day. The November 6 disclosure is a striking reminder that some of blockchain's largest financial use cases are institutional plumbing rather than publicly traded tokens. It also needs context: a month of cumulative repo activity is a flow measure, not $7.6 trillion of newly created blockchain assets.

Repurchase agreements are short-term financing arrangements in which securities are sold with an agreement to repurchase them, often against cash collateral. They are a major part of the funding market for banks and dealers. Broadridge's figure represents cumulative transaction processing through its DLR system during October, while the average daily figure gives a sense of ongoing throughput. It should not be mistaken for assets permanently locked in a protocol or a standalone market capitalization. Repeated financing transactions can generate large summed volume even while the underlying collateral turns over.

Repo involves collateral records, cash movement, timing, reconciliations and multiple operational teams. A shared transaction environment can reduce disagreements about the state of a deal and help participants coordinate settlement. That is an attractive use case for distributed infrastructure precisely because the counterparties may already be regulated financial institutions that need detailed permissions and controls. Broadridge's announcement presents DLR as a production platform, rather than a proof of concept. Still, the release does not by itself quantify net cost savings for individual users or independently verify every reported operational benefit.

Broadridge is using the DLR experience to promote its DLX platform, which it says supports issuance, trading, settlement, financing and asset servicing. This is a commercial strategy to connect workflows that are currently separate. A tokenized asset is more useful if it can be financed, transferred, serviced and reported without expensive custom integrations. The difficulty is coordination with existing custody, legal rights and market infrastructure. Moving one record onchain does not magically resolve differences between firms' processes, and institutional adoption may continue to favor permissioned arrangements.

The October number suggests substantial existing demand for shared-ledger settlement in securities financing. It does not mean all traditional repo has moved onto a blockchain, nor does it imply that users can trade the underlying collateral publicly. Differences between tokenized records, ownership registers and conventional settlement obligations can be legally significant. Readers should look for comparable periods, the number and diversity of participating institutions, operational resilience and the share of transactions that run without manual intervention. Those indicators help distinguish a very large gross number from lasting efficiency gains.

Broadridge expects tokenized finance to extend further through normal market operations in 2027. The most revealing milestones will be independent institutional adoption and recurring transaction volume across multiple product types. For crypto investors, the lesson is to separate blockchain use as infrastructure from token speculation. A huge processing volume can demonstrate a serious enterprise application without creating direct demand for a liquid crypto token.

The address was previously considered the most profitable one on Hyperliquid. However, the recent market downturn changed that, and the trader is now facing a net loss of $3.3 million.

The trader's Ethereum long position includes 30,282 ETH worth around $55.46 million, with a liquidation price of $1,740.

The trader also holds a 550,000 SOL long with 10x leverage. The position will be fully liquidated if the price of Solana falls to $65.6.

Besides, the trader holds 35.03 million XRP worth around $35 million, with a liquidation price of $0.94.

The selling of these positions is already putting pressure on the prices of all three cryptocurrencies.

In September 2025, UXLINK, a crypto social network with Telegram integration, suffered a hacker attack.

The attackers exploited the project's multisig infrastructure, which allowed them to drain the project's treasury and mint new tokens.

The total damage from the exploit and the subsequent crash of the UXLINK token price was estimated at around $42 million.

In August 2026, an anonymous trader deposited $11.54 million USDC on Hyperliquid.

According to EmberCN, the wallet that was used to pay gas fees for the trader received ETH from addresses that had previously received stolen UXLINK funds.

Since then, the trader has closed five profitable trades with a net gain of $5.71 million.

At the end of October, the trader was still holding $5.6 million in unrealized profit on the Ethereum position.

The recent market downturn erased that profit, and most of the trader's funds are now at risk of liquidation.

#5193. Dinari Adds Broadridge Voting Rails to Tokenized US Shares

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

TL;DR: Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure.

Tokenized stocks have often promised easier access and faster settlement, but a less glamorous question keeps surfacing: can the holder vote? Broadridge and Dinari announced an integration on November 5 that aims to connect eligible holders of Dinari's dShares to established proxy-voting infrastructure. The development highlights shareholder governance as a core feature of credible tokenization, not an optional extra on a trading app.

According to the companies, eligible dShare holders can exercise voting rights associated with the underlying US equities through Broadridge's proxy systems. Those votes are intended to enter the same formal processes used by traditional shareholders. This is more concrete than giving token holders a separate community poll about a company. Shareholder resolutions, board elections and other corporate actions depend on recognized ownership records, deadlines and entitlement calculations. The release describes an integration of these processes, although it does not publish a full end-to-end test record for each supported company.

A user buying exposure to a company's share may assume the resulting token comes with the same rights as a share in a conventional brokerage account. That assumption is dangerous unless the product's legal structure supports it. Some tokens are claims on intermediaries, while others are issued and serviced in ways designed to preserve shareholder entitlements. Dinari's integration addresses part of that problem by moving voting instructions through established channels. Investors should still verify which tokens qualify, whether voting is available in their jurisdiction and how any intermediary custody arrangements affect their position.

Broadridge already handles a large volume of investor communications and governance workflows in traditional markets. Connecting these systems to a tokenized product can be more practical than reconstructing every corporate-action process from scratch. That matters because an issuer cannot simply ignore events such as stock splits, tender offers or changes in the shareholder register. There may also be timing conflicts between token transfer windows and voting record dates. The harder task is keeping balances, entitlements and instruction chains aligned as holders move between wallets and supported intermediaries.

An improved voting experience does not automatically make a tokenized share freely transferable, exchange-listed or protected identically in every jurisdiction. Eligibility, investor verification and local securities rules may still apply. Likewise, a voting feature says little about trading liquidity or the robustness of the underlying custody model. Broadridge and Dinari's announcement is best understood as one part of the market's operational maturation. It makes a necessary ownership function more visible, but cannot settle every legal or commercial question around tokenized equities.

Useful evidence would include the number of supported issuers, actual voting participation by eligible holders, records of successful proxy delivery and support for other corporate actions. For asset managers and platforms considering tokenized stock distribution, governance infrastructure is a test of whether the product behaves like an investment or merely tracks its price. That distinction will become more important as institutions offer these instruments to a broader audience.

Primary source: Broadridge and Dinari joint release. For additional context, see NewsBTC’s coverage of transfer-agent participation in tokenized stock infrastructure.

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Cardano (ADA) has entered epoch 666, yet another milestone for the blockchain, which has been live since its launch in September 2017.

The number has drawn attention for its connection to the biblical 666, but the development also points to the Cardano network's basic timekeeping and staking mechanism.

Popular Cardano blockchain explorer Cexplorer displays that epoch 666 started on Nov. 5, 2026, and is expected to end on Nov. 10, with 1 day and 10 hours left to close. The milestone marks another five-day cycle finished in Cardano's long-running proof-of-stake system.

Cardano divides its operation into epochs, which are five days long and consist of 432,000 one-second slots. The importance of epoch 666 is largely symbolic and not technical, as it does not coincide with any major protocol upgrades or hard forks. But the number 666 has merely provided an interesting talking point for the Cardano community.

In a separate milestone, the Cardano network has processed over 127,000,000 transactions on mainnet. According to Cexplorer data, Cardano has recorded a total of 127,203,164 transactions.

In upgrade news, DijkstraNet, the Dijkstra hard fork testnet, has been hard forked to protocol version 12 and is now available for testing and integration against the full Dijkstra feature set, with the exception of Linear Leios.

Node 11.2 was pre-released on October 28 and successfully used to transition DijkstraNet into the Dijkstra era, and DB Sync 13.8.0.0 was released for all networks.

In separate upgrade news, Midnight has completed its upgrade from Ledger 8 to Ledger 9, bringing new capabilities for developers alongside security, compatibility, and performance improvements across the network.

Ledger 9 introduces native support for widely used cryptographic standards including ECDSA and Keccak-256, expands wallet and custody compatibility, and enables contracts to interact directly with one another.

Keccak-256 is the standard algorithm that Ethereum uses to scramble data into fixed-length cryptographic fingerprints. ECDSA is the standard digital signature method that networks like Bitcoin and Ethereum use to prove ownership of a specific wallet address.

#5190. Nigeria tells dollar-stablecoin issuers: go local or lose retail access

Retail dollar stablecoins need Nigerian issuers, local licenses and token approval. Existing operators need express interim permission during the transition.

Nigeria’s central bank now requires dollar-pegged stablecoins offered to retail customers to be issued by locally incorporated, licensed entities and receive token approval. The rules took effect November 5, 2026, with a conditional 180-day application transition for existing operators. Continued access for foreign-currency stablecoin arrangements during assessment requires express permission from the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN).

The CBN regulations classify foreign-currency stablecoins as Class 2. Section 6.5 requires a Nigerian-incorporated entity holding a Foreign Currency Issuer License (Class 2), alongside approval of the token itself.

A foreign license, regulatory status or agreement with a Nigerian intermediary cannot substitute for those approvals. The rules reach regulated activities directed at people in Nigeria even when the provider has no physical presence there.

Issuers and service providers face distinct approval requirements. Non-issuance service licenses or authorizations do not permit stablecoin issuance, while issuer applicants must establish a staffed Nigerian office and effective local management before final licensing, including a resident chief compliance officer.

The framework makes a narrow exception to local issuance. Section 11.10.17 allows the CBN to recognize a foreign-issued stablecoin solely for expressly approved wholesale cross-border settlement. That route excludes offerings to Nigerian retail customers, so it does not provide a substitute for the retail licensing requirements.

Approval also has limits on domestic use. Class 2 Token Approval does not authorize settling, pricing or discharging a naira-denominated domestic obligation unless applicable foreign-exchange or other law expressly permits it.

The regulations preserve the Securities and Exchange Commission’s statutory jurisdiction and do not automatically cancel approvals under other Nigerian frameworks. An existing principal license nevertheless does not remove the need for express CBN approval for non-security virtual asset services.

Section 54.1 gives existing operators 180 calendar days from commencement to submit a complete application for the appropriate license or authorization. They may continue only at their existing scale and subject to the CBN’s interim conditions.

The transition also requires registration with the bank within 30 days and supervisory reporting within 60 days, or an earlier prescribed period. Anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and counter-proliferation financing requirements apply from commencement.

For existing Class 2 arrangements, the CBN will assess Nigerian incorporation, issuer licensing and service-provider approvals. Continued access during that assessment requires the bank’s express interim permission and does not create a permanent exemption. Submitting an application alone therefore does not establish permission to keep serving the market.

Operators that miss the application deadline must cease operating until the necessary license or authorization is obtained.

#5187. Ondo Claims $4B in Tokenized Assets as RWA Market Gains Institutional Depth

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data.

Ondo Finance says its tokenized real-world-asset products have crossed $4 billion in value, with 484 distinct assets and more than 565,000 onchain holders. The figures appear in a corrected November 5 company announcement citing RWA.xyz data. They illustrate how tokenized finance is broadening beyond a small set of Treasury products, but the definitions behind a ranking matter as much as the impressive headline figure.

The corrected release says Ondo ranks first among 203 platforms tracked by RWA.xyz by the market capitalization of tokenized products and accounts for roughly a tenth of non-stablecoin RWA value. The comparison excludes stablecoins and uses the data provider's classification of assets and platforms. Readers should not confuse it with Ondo's revenue, cash on its balance sheet, net inflows in a single day or the trading volume of the ONDO token. Tokenized product value can also move with prices and redemptions, so the number should be treated as a dated snapshot rather than an immutable milestone.

The category now spans short-term government debt, funds, equities and other exposures offered through various legal and custody structures. Those instruments may all be called real-world assets while providing very different rights, liquidity and redemption procedures. A tokenized money market interest can behave unlike a tokenized stock, and neither should be analyzed simply as an unsecured crypto token. The key question is what claim the holder owns, who maintains the legal records and how a user receives the underlying value when a transaction or redemption is requested.

Issuing a blockchain representation is relatively straightforward compared with making it useful to investors and institutions. Platforms need identity checks, compliant distribution, secondary transfer controls, custody arrangements and ongoing servicing. The scale reported by Ondo suggests that these practical layers have become commercially significant. Yet a large holder count does not disclose how assets are concentrated, whether addresses represent individuals or intermediaries, or what proportion trades regularly. A platform can be large by outstanding value while some products remain relatively illiquid.

Ondo issued this information as a correction, making it particularly important to use the complete revised text rather than an earlier headline copied across aggregators. Rankings also depend on the measurement date and definitions used by the data provider. A later expansion of coverage or reclassification could change relative positions without any shift in underlying user demand. Readers should therefore seek source methodology and product-level information before interpreting a top ranking as evidence of an uncontested or permanent market lead.

The strongest sign of maturation will be whether tokenized products are used in ordinary financial workflows: collateral management, settlement, portfolio allocation and redemptions. Transparent asset backing, enforceable rights and resilient operations will matter more than product count alone. Ondo's milestone is a useful indicator of scale, provided it is presented as a company-reported snapshot of tokenized assets rather than a promise about future returns or market dominance.

Telegram CEO Pavel Durov has shared new metrics on the Gram wallet integration in the messenger.

According to Durov, over the last 48 hours alone, users activated more than 700,000 non-custodial Gram wallets.

The screenshot shared by the Telegram CEO shows more than 329,000 new addresses a day. According to GRAM documentation, a wallet is created automatically when a user receives their first token transfer.

700K+ self-custodial wallets created on Telegram in the last 48 hours alone. Adoption spreads virally: a wallet activates the moment someone receives Grams. The crypto revolution is going strong. https://t.co/JPO2KVMip0

The growth comes after a series of changes Telegram made to the TON network earlier this year under Durov's "Make TON Great Again" campaign.

#5184. US drops a proposed crypto rule. Europe can still hold up your $500 transfer

The US has withdrawn its proposed $250 transfer threshold, but missing identity information can still hold up even a $500 payment at an EU exchange.

FinCEN, the U.S. financial-crime regulator, and the Federal Reserve announced Nov. 6 that they are withdrawing a plan to expand transfer-data duties to cross-border payments as small as $250. Existing U.S. requirements remain, alongside EU information checks that can affect even a $500 crypto payment.

An illustrative $500 customer transfer from a U.S. exchange to an EU exchange shows the limit of the retreat. It is below the U.S. Travel Rule's $3,000 threshold, but the receiving exchange's EU obligations can still prevent the recipient from accessing the assets until required information is supplied.

The joint withdrawal notice was published in the Federal Register on Nov. 9, with withdrawal effective that day. FinCEN's Nov. 6 announcement confirmed the decision. The proposed $250 threshold never took effect through this rulemaking.

The October 2020 proposal would have lowered the threshold for specified recordkeeping and information-transmission duties from $3,000 to $250 for transfers beginning or ending outside the United States.

The existing Recordkeeping Rule requires covered institutions to collect and retain transfer information, while the Travel Rule requires information to pass to other institutions in the payment chain. The joint notice describes the current threshold as $3,000 or more. Withdrawing the proposal avoids extending those duties into the lower-value band.

The agencies cite the passage of more than five years, the value of further public feedback and changes in virtual-currency markets and legal frameworks. They say any future similar amendments should reflect those developments.

Existing crypto compliance duties continue. FinCEN's 2019 virtual-currency guidance says qualifying convertible-virtual-currency transfers of $3,000 or more can trigger Travel Rule requirements. Covered money transmitters also retain applicable anti-money-laundering programs, customer-identification controls, recordkeeping, monitoring and reporting obligations.

The EU's crypto-transfer regulation, applicable since Dec. 30, 2024, covers customer transfers involving a crypto-asset service provider with its registered office in the EU. Its information requirements have no general exemption for small crypto transfers. The regulation explains that crypto transfers should face the same requirements regardless of amount or whether they are domestic or cross-border.

For the hypothetical $500 payment, assume the receiving exchange is an EU-registered provider serving a customer. The relevant duties here belong to the EU receiving provider; the U.S. exchange's own obligations are governed separately.

On a risk-sensitive basis, request required information before availability, or reject/return. Act without undue delay.

The U.S. retreat leaves the EU exchange's information and recipient-verification requirements intact.

Scope: ordinary customer exchange-to-exchange crypto transfer with an EU-registered receiving provider. Other controls may apply. The separate self-hosted-address test and provider-free P2P exemption are outside this diagram. No processing-time or failure estimate.

Qualitative illustration from the joint notice, FinCEN CVC guidance and EU Articles 2,14-17. $500 is hypothetical, not an observed payment. Arrows show responsibilities and information flow, not speed, volume or legal reach over a US-only sender.

Scope: ordinary customer exchange-to-exchange crypto transfer with an EU-registered receiving provider. Other controls may apply. The separate self-hosted-address test and provider-free P2P exemption are outside this diagram. No processing-time or failure estimate.

Article 14 specifies sender and recipient names, relevant blockchain addresses and applicable crypto-account identifiers. Sender information also includes an address and country, official document number and customer identification number, or alternatively a date and place of birth. Additional legal-entity identifiers are conditional.

Providers can exchange that information in secure messages separate from the blockchain transaction. The EU receiving provider must detect missing information and verify recipient information before making the assets available; qualifying previous identity verification can satisfy the latter check.

If required details are missing or incomplete, Article 17 requires the receiving provider to act on a risk-sensitive basis and without undue delay. It must reject or return the transfer, or request the required information before making the assets available. Its procedures can include suspension.

That is how blockchain arrival and access to funds can diverge: the assets can arrive while the exchange still needs information before releasing them to its customer.

The regulation adds an ownership-or-control assessment for transfers exceeding €1,000 to or from self-hosted addresses. Smaller transfers still face the applicable information requirements. The exchange-to-exchange example falls under those general rules rather than this self-hosted-address test.

Scope matters, too. Person-to-person crypto transfers without a service provider fall outside the regulation, as do transfers where both providers act on their own behalf. An ordinary customer payment between exchanges remains within the provider-based framework.

The European Banking Authority's applicable guidelines address detecting missing information and managing transfers that lack it.

#5183. Schroders Emerging-Market Bond Strategy Moves Onto Solana Through Centrifuge

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

TL;DR: Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure.

Schroders is bringing an emerging-market bond strategy into the tokenized fund market through Centrifuge on Solana. The November 4 announcement concerns the Schroder International Selection Fund Emerging Market Bond strategy, with Centrifuge providing onchain infrastructure. It is notable because the assets are not a cryptocurrency basket: investors are being offered a blockchain-native route to a conventional, actively managed fixed-income strategy with its own risks and investment processes.

Centrifuge says the initiative will introduce tokenized exposure to the Schroders emerging-market bond fund. Schroders manages more than $1 trillion in assets across its business, according to the announcement, and has decades of experience investing in debt issued by emerging-market governments and companies. That corporate scale provides context for the partnership; it is not an estimate of how much capital has entered this particular onchain fund. The launch represents Schroders' first Solana deployment, a specific milestone that should not be confused with a wholesale shift of the manager's portfolios to public blockchains.

Emerging-market bonds can offer access to currencies, credit risks and interest-rate conditions very different from those facing US Treasury bills. The underlying portfolio may be affected by sovereign finances, corporate defaults, currency movements and changes in global borrowing costs. Tokenization does not eliminate those exposures. It changes how interests in an investment strategy can be issued, recorded, distributed or serviced. Investors need to understand the fund's legal structure, eligibility, fees, dealing arrangements and the precise way token holdings map to recognized ownership. Those details ultimately determine whether the product meets their requirements.

Solana's appeal to financial product developers includes its transaction throughput and low per-transaction fees, while Centrifuge focuses on the specialist infrastructure needed to operate tokenized funds. The challenge is making asset management routines work with a public network without losing compliance controls. Fund subscriptions, redemptions, transfer restrictions and investor records must align with the legally constituted vehicle. A fast chain is helpful, but it cannot replace the fund administrator, custodian or manager. Operational success depends on the quality of those connections, not simply on the number of transactions the blockchain can process.

Much of the early RWA market concentrated on tokenized cash and short-dated US government debt. An actively managed emerging-market bond strategy is a different proposition because valuation, liquidity and portfolio turnover can be more complicated. A market may be open at all hours even when underlying bonds trade within narrower windows. That difference makes pricing and redemption policies essential. The value proposition could be broader distribution and improved processing, but investors should not infer that every share can be redeemed instantly or that tokenization creates round-the-clock liquidity in the underlying securities.

The next useful evidence would include an initial live issuance, assets held in the tokenized structure, participating distributors, supported jurisdictions and how subscriptions and redemptions actually settle. Over time, the question is whether blockchain infrastructure improves operational efficiency and attracts new investors without weakening fund protections. The announcement is a meaningful institutional experiment, but the practical success of the fund will rest on ordinary asset-management disciplines as much as on Solana technology.

#5180. Bitcoin Lightning’s security update shuts one door. A critical Linux flaw remains

LND’s October 30 update blocks a demonstrated attack route, but affected, unpatched Linux hosts still need a kernel fix and reboot.

Bitcoin Lightning operators running an affected, unpatched Linux kernel remain exposed to a critical vulnerability after upgrading LND, the software used to operate their payment nodes.

Its October 30 releases, v0.20.7-beta and v0.21.6-beta, disable Multipath TCP, or MPTCP, listeners by default. That closes the demonstrated CVE-2026-98432 route through those listeners. It leaves the kernel flaw in place and does not cover other services on the same machine.

Another exposed MPTCP service on the same unpatched machine can preserve the demonstrated route, even after LND’s default listeners have changed.

The flaw involves freed memory being used during IPv4 TCP connection handling in Linux and can allow an attacker to run code on an affected host. Ubuntu assigns it a critical CVSS 3.1 score of 9.8.

LND’s operator notes say Go 1.24 and later enabled MPTCP listeners by default on Linux, which LND 0.21.x consequently exposed on its peer, gRPC and REST ports. These include the node’s connections to other nodes and its application interfaces.

The Go Security Team’s advisory explains why that change cannot finish the job. The demonstrated exploit requires an exposed MPTCP listener, but the kernel bug is broader. Similar attacks against systems without MPTCP listeners may be possible; the advisory does not establish a demonstrated non-MPTCP exploit.

Go also warns that disabling MPTCP one program at a time is fragile. A single remaining exposed listener leaves the system vulnerable to that route, and explicit socket settings can override Go’s default configuration.

The advisories describe a demonstrated Linux exploit, not evidence that attackers used this flaw against LND nodes or stole Bitcoin.

CryptoSlate previously covered the same CVE’s implications for Solana validators. The Core Lightning channel and remote-command fixes reported November 6 concern separate application flaws.

The Ubuntu tracker, checked November 9 and last updated November 7, still labeled the standard linux package for Ubuntu 24.04 LTS vulnerable, with work in progress in 6.8.0-149.149. Its Ubuntu 22.04 LTS entry carried the same status for 5.15.0-203.213.

Patch availability varies by package. In its November 2 advisory, Canonical said kernel fixes for this CVE were available in the -proposed repository for users who run their own kernel acceptance tests, while qualification testing continued.

Ubuntu’s work-in-progress newsletter for November 1–7 also said some releases, including 24.04, had advanced to -updates. That broader note does not identify every kernel variant. Operators therefore need to check the available update for their exact kernel package rather than infer availability from the Ubuntu release name alone.

The tracker illustrates the distinction: it lists the standard Ubuntu 26.10 linux package as fixed in 7.3.0-10.10, while cloud, hardware-enablement and other kernel variants have separate entries. A fixed status for one package cannot settle the status of another.

LND maintainers recommend upgrading the application, disabling MPTCP on the host, and installing a patched kernel as soon as the distribution makes one available.

Their guidance uses sudo sysctl -w net.mptcp.enabled=0 for the host setting, with a persistent configuration to retain it. The setting applies per network namespace, so Docker deployments need separate attention to the container’s network configuration. Changing the host alone is not a substitute for checking that scope.

Operators who cannot upgrade LND immediately can start their existing binary with GODEBUG=multipathtcp=0 to disable Go’s default MPTCP listeners. Maintainers warn against re-enabling that default before patching the kernel.

Canonical advises checking the kernel actually running with uname -r. After installing its kernel security update, a reboot is required. An upgraded LND binary and an installed kernel package are different milestones; completing the operating-system repair requires running the patched kernel.

#5179. Binance to shut down its Bitcoin mining pool – Despite $233M in Q3 revenue

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Binance is set to shut down its Bitcoin [BTC] mining pool on the 10th of November. However, the decision in no sense means the crypto exchange is exiting Bitcoin mining altogether.

Launched in April 2020, Binane pool allowed independent miners to combine their computing power and receive more predictable mining rewards. However, its influence has gradually diminished.

According to data by mempool.space, Binance [BNB] Pool’s hashrate index fell from approximately 26 exahashes per second (EH/s) in December 2025 to 9.2 EH/s in October 2026.

In other words, there was a decline of roughly 65%, taking its estimated share of Bitcoin’s network hashrate from 2.3% to less than 1%.

At the same time, Binance Pool mined just one block in the seven-day period, representing approximately 0.11% of the 925 blocks discovered across the Bitcoin network. In fact, it recorded zero blocks in the latest 24 hours.

However, to date it has mined 22,213 blocks, accounting for approximately 2.28% of all Bitcoin blocks.

This comes as there is also a broader economic challenge facing the Bitcoin mining industry. Following the April 2024 halving, the block subsidy dropped from 6.25 BTC to 3.125 BTC, reducing the amount of newly issued Bitcoin miners receive for producing blocks.

Meanwhile, competitors including Foundry USA, AntPool, and F2Pool have become particularly dominant, together accounting for a substantial share of recent Bitcoin block discoveries.

Another important factor is the changing direction of the broader mining industry. Several publicly traded Bitcoin miners have started exploring artificial intelligence (AI) and high-performance computing (HPC) infrastructure as alternative revenue sources.

Lastly, Bitcoin miner outflows were also fluctuating throughout 2026, with most daily readings remaining between 5,000 and 10,000 BTC.

However, November 2026 is notable for the absence of a sustained surge in selling activity. Daily outflows have mostly remained moderate, with the index standing at 6,800 BTC at press time.

At the same time, Bitcoin’s price has weakened from around $80,000 in late October to approximately $74,200 at press time.

Together, these figures strongly suggest that Binance Pool’s mining activity had fallen considerably ahead of its scheduled November 10 shutdown.

Besides this, Core Scientific, once the largest Bitcoin [BTC] miner, also announced its plans to shut down its Bitcoin mining by Q4 2026 despite Q3 revenue hitting $233 million.

#5178. Online Gaming, Crypto Payments and On-Chain Games Are Different Categories

Home » Uncategorized » Online Gaming, Crypto Payments and On-Chain Games Are Different Categories

Online gaming, crypto payments, and blockchain gaming are not the same thing. Learn how to distinguish payment methods, game mechanics, and on-chain execution when evaluating crypto-enabled gaming platforms.

A wallet button beside a game does not explain where its rules run. A token ticker does not reveal who maintains the game state. Even a transaction recorded on a blockchain may describe a payment rather than a move inside the game. For readers assessing gaming products, these details matter because three separate ideas are often compressed into one label: access through the internet, payment with cryptocurrency, and execution on a blockchain.

An online game uses a network connection for some part of its operation. That could involve downloading content, joining a match, checking an account, or sending actions to a server. The browser or installed app supplies the interface, while processing can be divided between the player’s device and remote systems.

None of those arrangements requires a blockchain. A server can maintain account balances and game records in an ordinary database. A browser can display animation produced locally while showing information returned by that server. The visual experience alone reveals little about the underlying architecture.

This is also why an app download and browser access do not define opposing financial models. Either interface can connect to a conventional payment system, a crypto payment service, or a mixture of both. Distribution tells you how the product reaches the player. It does not identify the system that records ownership or enforces its rules.

DailyCoin’s analysis of DeFi front ends and smart contracts examines the separation between a website and the programs it accesses. The same distinction helps when assessing a game: its interface and the system executing its rules need to be identified separately.

Accepting cryptocurrency adds a payment method. A service might receive an asset directly or work through a payment processor that monitors transfers and updates the service’s account records. The asset received and the balance displayed to the customer need not be represented in the same way.

For example, a hypothetical platform could accept a token transfer and then record a corresponding account credit in its own database. Subsequent game actions could take place entirely within that platform’s existing infrastructure. The blockchain transfer and the account credit would be connected operationally, but they would remain separate records.

A transaction hash can help identify the transfer. It does not, by itself, reveal the logic used to calculate an unrelated game result. To understand the product, the next question is what happened after payment: was only a balance updated, or did a transaction call code that changed the game’s state?

Casino catalogs illustrate why these labels need to stay precise. Slots are identified by their reel or grid layouts, symbols, paylines, and feature rules. Classic slots, video slots, and progressive jackpot formats describe aspects of the game or prize structure. Those descriptions do not specify a blockchain network.

Consider how little a slot’s format tells us about its payment infrastructure. A payline defines which symbol positions form a combination, and a bonus rule defines what triggers an additional feature. Neither tells us how a deposit reaches the account or where the outcome calculation runs. Spin Casino’s description of online slots in Canada focuses on those game formats and mechanics. It belongs to the product-description layer of the analysis, separate from evidence about a wallet integration or a blockchain contract.

That separation prevents a familiar classification error: treating a digital casino game as an on-chain game simply because both are discussed alongside cryptocurrency. To establish a blockchain connection, identify the actual payment flow, asset record or executed game action. The slot label alone supplies none of those details.

The same discipline applies to a product described as a blockchain game. That label could refer to tokenized items while the match itself runs on a server. An ownership record and a record of the rules being executed are different kinds of evidence.

To understand on-chain gameplay, look for the programs that govern actions and store their consequences. Ethereum’s introduction to smart contracts describes contracts as code and state at an address on the blockchain. Transactions can call their functions, and execution follows the programmed rules.

In a hypothetical turn-based game, a contract could check whose turn it is, determine whether a move is permitted, and update the board. Recording only a collectible associated with that game would be a narrower use of the technology. The board and its rules might still be managed elsewhere.

Products can also combine these approaches. Some assets or actions may be recorded on-chain while other systems remain on servers. The interface can stay off-chain even when the underlying game logic runs in contracts. A claim of fully on-chain gameplay therefore needs a clear account of which rules and state are included, plus any outside data on which they depend.

When reading a product description, follow one action from start to finish. Identify what the player submits, which system processes it, and where the resulting change is recorded. That gives “online,” “crypto-enabled,” and “on-chain” concrete meanings that a logo, wallet connection, or token name cannot supply.

#5177. Schiff: Saylor's STRC Is 'Dead'

Earlier today, gold bug Peter Schiff claimed that Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor was trying to prop up the floundering investment product by carrying out heavy stock buybacks.

"Michael, STRC is dead. You have been keeping it alive on artificial life support with your buybacks," he wrote.

According to Schiff, Strategy is running out of money to prop up its preferred stock. The ongoing Bitcoin market crash is going to aggravate the situation even further, he argued.

"But you're running out of cash. And the selling pressure on STRC will increase as Bitcoin crashes," Schiff wrote.

The Bitcoin bear went on to criticize the generous 12% annualized dividend yield of STRC, saying that ultimately the yield wouldn't be enough to cover the risks of the product.

"It won't be nearly enough yield to cover the risk. 12%," he warned.

The stern comments from Schiff followed a typical bullish tweet from Saylor. In his post, Saylor claimed that AI could not mint new Bitcoin.

"AI can make me rap. It can't print Bitcoin," the cofounder of Strategy wrote.

Strategy's Variable Rate Series A Perpetual Stretch Preferred Stock (STRC) seeks to provide regular dividend income to investors while trading near its $100 face value.

Currently, STRC offers a 12% annual dividend yield, which Strategy has been working to keep steady in order to keep the stock trading near its face value.

However, maintaining the price stability of STRC has come at a big cost.

In its Q3 financial results on Oct. 29, Strategy reported that the firm had spent a total of $2.04 billion on repurchases of STRC as of Oct. 25.

Describing the heavy buybacks as a success, the firm said it had successfully put STRC on the road to financial recovery.

However, these buybacks have come under fire from Schiff, who questions whether the firm can keep propping up investor demand by repurchasing its shares forever.

In spite of the bearish comments from Schiff, Strategy isn't budging on its strategy of ramping up its Bitcoin holdings.

The firm's recent regulatory filing shows that Strategy bought another 1,036 BTC between Nov. 2 and Nov. 8.

The total cost of these purchases is estimated to be $81.9 million, with an average purchase price of $79,012 per BTC.

With the latest purchase, Strategy now holds an eye-watering 850,364 BTC.

#5176. Zcash Upgrade Could Lock $16 Million in Crypto Forever

Zcash Upgrade Could Lock $16 Million in Crypto Forever

At recent market prices, those holdings represent roughly $15 million to $16 million that could become effectively frozen when the network activates its NU7 upgrade.

“NU7 (block 3,543,405) makes v4 transactions invalid, so what remains in Sprout is unspendable: frozen, not burned,” Zecstats says in its information card for Sprout.

The upgrade is scheduled for block 3,543,405, expected Thursday evening in the United States. The exact deadline depends on how quickly the blockchain processes new blocks, rather than a predetermined clock time.

Unlike Bitcoin, where transactions are generally visible to anyone examining the blockchain, Zcash allows users to conceal transaction amounts and the addresses involved. It accomplishes this through technology called zero-knowledge proofs, which can verify that a transaction is valid without revealing its private details.

NU7 changes that by eliminating version-4 transactions, the only format capable of moving coins out of Sprout. According to the network's technical specification, transactions using that format will become invalid after activation.

The decision addresses a problem familiar to anyone maintaining old software: supporting obsolete technology creates additional complexity and potential security vulnerabilities.

Developers haven't technically destroyed the coins. They will continue counting toward Zcash's circulating issuance calculations, and a future network upgrade could theoretically restore access, but that is not guaranteed, and the team has not shown any interest in doing so.

In fact, the specification explicitly warns that spending those funds may never be re-enabled.

Legacy holders are the people most exposed to the change. Anyone whose ZEC remains in Sprout must move it through a compatible withdrawal mechanism before the upgrade activates, or risk losing access indefinitely.

Sprout addresses begin with "zc," which can help users recognize old wallet records. Regular ZEC holders using modern supported wallets do not need to migrate their coins out of Sprout, although keeping wallet software updated remains important.

The blockchain also cannot reveal who owns the remaining Sprout balance, meaning nobody knows how much belongs to active users and how much is already inaccessible because its owners lost their keys.

Meanwhile, NU7 brings a benefit for everyone else: Zcash's target block interval falls from 75 seconds to 25 seconds, meaning transactions should receive their first confirmation approximately three times faster, according to the Zcash Foundation.

For Sprout holders, however, the relevant number is block 3,543,405 which will happen later today. As of the time of publication, the latest available block is 3,543,027. Once the network reaches block 3,543,405, any remaining coins in the old pool will be frozen under the new rules.

#5175. Ethereum loses 2024 gains – Is Vitalik Buterin rethinking ETH’s long-term value?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Ethereum’s [ETH] long-term investment case has been relatively weaker compared to Bitcoin.

On an annual basis, ETH has fallen nearly 30% this year, dragging its price down to $1.5k levels, and eliminating all the gains made throughout 2024 and 2025. What’s more, the altcoin is currently trading nearly 10% “lower” than it was at the start of 2024, highlighting its weak cycle-wide returns.

Bitcoin, on the other hand, has been much more resilient. After correcting 15% in 2026, BTC is still trading above 75% higher from its 2024 starting point, representing a much better long term ROI. The weakness extends into the ETH/BTC ratio, which is down over 16%, heading towards a fifth consecutive bearish annual candle. The ratio also trades around 60% below its 2024 opening level.

In essence, Bitcoin has maintained a clear lead in the long-term investment narrative.

According to AMBCrypto, this is where Vitalik Buterin’s recent X post comes into play. For years, Ethereum’s investment thesis has revolved around its deflationary model, lower gas fees, and token-burn mechanics. The idea was to strengthen ETH’s value proposition through reduced supply and increased network activity.

However, ETH’s continued underperformance relative to BTC raises questions about how well this supply-driven narrative is translating into price action. In this light, Buterin’s new SOV thesis may be an attempt to drive this change in investment thesis. By highlighting Ethereumas a “store of value,” Buterin might be trying to shift ETH’s investment thesis to that of being a long-term value asset.

The reason behind Vitalik Buterin’s changing approach is becoming clearer from on-chain data.

According to on-chain data, ETH burns have declined by 98.8% from $3.548 billion in 2022 to just $42.8 million in 2026. This reduces how much of the Ethereum supply is being taken out of circulation, therefore undermining the deflationary narrative. This means the emphasis will shift to demand. Ethereum may derive more of its long-term value from becoming a collateral rather than from supply reduction through token burns.

Against this backdrop, recent whale activity adds another layer to ETH’s outlook. According to Onchain Lens, a large holder has withdrawn 16,580 ETH from Binance. However, whale accumulation might not be enough to compensate for a lack of staking demand. According to ValidatorQueue, the amount of ETH waiting to be staked has been on a downtrend since peaking at 4 million ETH in February.

This is where Buterin’s new store-of-value (SOV) narrative becomes important.

With staking demand declining, Ethereum’s collateral use case could also come under pressure. As ETH acts as collateral for loans, DeFi positions and overall financial activity within the ecosystem, a continued decrease in demand to hold and use ETH as collateral could put downward pressure on its long-term utility.

From this perspective, Vitalik Buterin’s latest post could be a key moment in reshaping Ethereum’s long-term investment case against Bitcoin.

#5174. North Korean Hackers Flip Stolen Binance Funds Into NEAR Meme Coins

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

North Korea's TraderTraitor group has started laundering funds stolen from Binance through newly created meme tokens, according to Elliptic.

The $6.4 billion Binance hack took place in October 2026 and was attributed to TraderTraitor.

According to Elliptic, the hackers have used this technique on Tron and NEAR, while a similar approach has appeared on Solana.

Between Nov. 5 and 7, 2026, the hackers launched at least six of these tokens on NEAR: FUK, OLCCL, MEILI, MMLI, DABI and SINU. Launching one cost around 25 NEAR (about $90).

According to Elliptic, the hackers paired each token with NEAR in a liquidity pool on a decentralized exchange (DEX). Wallets holding stolen NEAR deposited it into the pool and received the new token. A second set of wallets then sold the token back into the pool and withdrew NEAR.

This way, the funds never move directly from the wallets holding stolen assets to the receiving wallets.

According to Elliptic, the receiving wallets look like ordinary traders who sold a token at a profit.

Each token got typical meme branding, from monkeys to an image of Elon Musk under an "Elon 2028 President" banner. Elliptic noted that Musk is not linked to the tokens.

Each token was sold for the first time less than three hours after launch, and at least 75% of its trading took place within one day. None of the six tokens has traded since Nov. 8, and the creators of four of them withdrew the remaining liquidity on that day.

In total, 117,000 NEAR (about $421,000) moved through the scheme. Most of it then went into stablecoins or to a cross-chain bridge.

Elliptic noted that five of the six token creators received funds from a wallet that had been selling the previous token 2 to 13 minutes before the new launch, and in this way the operation funded itself.

The only outside activity was a few small purchases of FUK on its first day, which accounted for less than 1% of its volume, Elliptic said.

According to Elliptic, the on-chain trail stays public, and the technique makes tracing the funds slower. The hackers can also create many tokens and abandon each one after use.

In 2025, after the Bybit hack, the same scheme moved at least $24 million through Tron. In that case, the hackers paired a worthless token with a stablecoin.

In the Binance case, Elliptic identified a similar token on Tron on Nov. 2. On Nov. 3, stolen SOL was swapped into existing thinly traded tokens on Solana and then sold for USDC.

Elliptic said that so far only a small part of the stolen funds has gone through meme tokens. About 11.8 million NEAR from the theft has not moved yet, and at press time, NEAR is trading at $3.60, which puts these funds at around $42.4 million.

Elliptic also advises compliance teams to check funds coming from liquidity pools, especially pools with newly created tokens.

"Laundering is a race to move funds before they are flagged," Elliptic added.

#5173. Mercado Bitcoin Said Its Hack Was Contained, But Blockchain Data Tells a Different Story

Mercado Bitcoin Said Its Hack Was Contained, But Blockchain Data Tells a Different Story

An attacker drained Mercado Bitcoin-linked deposit addresses nearly four hours after the Brazilian exchange said it had contained a security breach, new blockchain research shows.

Bitquery's analysis, updated Thursday, traces more than $48 million in stolen assets across 11 blockchains. Its findings challenge the exchange's claim that it stopped the attack quickly.

The Bitcoin exchange announced at 9:56 a.m. Brazil time on November 2 that it had quickly contained the incident. Bitquery says 36,042 Ethereum customer deposit addresses were emptied between 9:27 a.m. and 1:56 p.m. Brazil time.

Those addresses held roughly $266,000, a small fraction of the total theft. But the attacker could still move those funds after the exchange’s announcement.

A customer deposit address works much like a personal receiving account for cryptocurrency. The exchange later gathers those coins into a shared online wallet, called a hot wallet, to process everyday transactions. Moving funds from a deposit address requires its private key, the secret that authorizes transfers.

Bitquery says the withdrawals were authorized directly by the deposit addresses, suggesting the attacker had access to their private keys or to a system capable of signing transactions on their behalf.

“That needs a key for each address, or a way into the system that signs for them,” the researchers explained. They warned that exchanges typically generate deposit keys from a single master key, meaning the attacker may still be able to access other customer addresses.

The amount stolen is also disputed. Initial estimates put the amount above $40 million, while Mercado Bitcoin's updated FAQ now puts affected assets at about $36.3 million. Bitquery estimates that $48.6 million was stolen across 11 blockchains.

Mercado Bitcoin's public updates have not explained the gap between its containment claim and the later transfers. The company assured customers it would cover user losses with its own funds.

Bitquery warns customers against reusing old deposit addresses until the exchange confirms they are safe. Mercado Bitcoin's reopening plan begins November 9 with balance viewing only; deposits, withdrawals and trading have no restart date.

#5170. Two Bitcoin miners reported nearly $2 billion in profit. The biggest boost wasn’t cash

Core Scientific and TeraWulf’s reported profits include large non-cash gains. Their operating results and construction cash flows tell different stories.

Core Scientific and TeraWulf reported nearly $1.9 billion of combined third-quarter profit as they shifted from Bitcoin mining toward data-center hosting for AI customers. Their earnings included $1.76 billion of pretax non-cash gains from revaluing financial instruments.

The November 5 Core Scientific disclosure and November 6 TeraWulf disclosure show different operating outcomes for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Core earned $72 million in operating income under U.S. accounting rules; TeraWulf recorded an $88 million operating loss. Core's operating result itself included a $19 million digital-asset fair-value gain. Hosting now supplies most of both companies' revenue, following their shift from Bitcoin mining toward computing leases. Assessing whether the conversions fund themselves requires the separate cash-flow and financing disclosures.

Core’s $1,178 million consolidated net income and TeraWulf’s $710 million add up to approximately $1.89 billion.

In Core's filing, the $1,034 million revaluation gain comprised $964 million on legacy Tranche 1 and Tranche 2 warrants, $69 million on the liability portion of an AMD warrant and $1 million on contingent value rights. Legacy instruments supplied the largest component of Core's gain.

Warrants give holders rights to buy shares. Core's AMD warrant accompanied July customer leases, with its issuance value recorded as an incentive reducing future lease revenue. Its liability portion is remeasured through earnings. Core attributed changes in its broader warrant and contingent-value line primarily to stock-price changes.

TeraWulf's $728 million gain came from revaluing Google warrants issued in exchange for credit support covering certain Fluidstack lease obligations. The credit support can help finance projects. Remeasurement raises reported earnings through a non-cash accounting entry.

The revaluation gains enter earnings before tax, while the net-income figures also reflect tax effects and other gains. Core also recorded a $106.5 million tax benefit, primarily from releasing part of a valuation allowance associated with its Polaris acquisition. TeraWulf recorded a $95 million gain on selling its Abernathy joint-venture stake.

Core Scientific and TeraWulf reported $1.89bn in consolidated Q3 net income alongside $1.76bn of pretax non-cash revaluation gains.

Legacy warrants supplied most of Core's $1.034bn pretax revaluation gain. Its AMD warrant is a separate lease-linked instrument.

Google warrants supporting Fluidstack leases produced TeraWulf's $728.4m non-cash gain. Credit support and cash proceeds are distinct.

Large accounting gains can lift net income while operating results diverge.

Net income is after tax; revaluation gains are before tax. Separate scales compare earnings and operating results. These measures differ from cash flow and cannot establish construction-funding adequacy.

Q3 ended September 30, 2026. USD millions. Reported figures rounded from filings. Net-income bars share a 0 to $1,200m scale; operating bars use a separate symmetric ±$100m scale. Core instrument gains sum to $1,034.358m before rounding. No pretax gain is subtracted from after-tax income.

Net income is after tax; revaluation gains are before tax. Separate scales compare earnings and operating results. These measures differ from cash flow and cannot establish construction-funding adequacy.

The difference also reaches per-share results: Core reported $3.42 basic earnings versus $0.47 diluted, while TeraWulf reported $1.42 basic earnings and a $0.03 diluted loss. The diluted calculations include warrant-gain reversals in the earnings used per share, alongside share-count adjustments.

Hosting growth is visible in both companies' sales. Core's colocation revenue reached $215 million out of $233 million in total sales, up from $137 million in the preceding quarter. Colocation gross profit was $128 million at a reported 60% margin.

TeraWulf generated $63 million of high-performance computing (HPC) lease revenue, approximately 83% of its $76 million total. Its $11 million HPC segment profit excludes expenses including corporate overhead and depreciation that enter consolidated operating results, giving it a different expense allocation from Core's colocation gross profit.

For the nine months ended September 30, Core generated $296 million of operating cash while spending $1,495 million on property, plant and equipment and another $677 million on asset acquisitions. Net financing cash inflow was $3,200 million.

Over that same nine-month period, TeraWulf used $179 million of operating cash and spent $2,231 million on plant and equipment purchases and deposits. It received $1,010 million of net financing cash, including approximately $1,200 million from common-stock issuance.

Core says conversions for hosting customer CoreWeave are largely funded by that customer. Development under its AMD and other cloud-customer arrangements will require additional external financing. It plans project-level bond financing. Management says existing liquidity plus anticipated funding sources support planned development and operating needs.

TeraWulf's Abernathy sale supplied $250 million of cash during Q3, distinct from the accounting gain; further installments remained expected. After quarter-end, it increased revolving-credit commitments to about $400 million, with an additional conditional, uncommitted $150 million expansion option. Its post-quarter November 4 Google credit support for leases with customer Anthropic concerns anticipated project financing. The Fluidstack warrants behind Q3's gain relate to a separate arrangement.

For the next phase, the operating split provides a more useful starting point than the combined profit: Core has reached positive operating income, while TeraWulf still reports an operating loss. Delivered hosting capacity, cash collections and financing commitments will determine how much of the construction bill the growing businesses can carry.

#5169. Charles Schwab Expands Crypto Trading to SOL, AVAX and LINK, XRP Not Included

American brokerage giant Charles Schwab has announced that it is expanding its crypto trading platform, Schwab Crypto, with the addition of Solana (SOL), Avalanche (AVAX) and Chainlink (LINK) for trading.

The three new coins expand the existing list of two cryptocurrencies, Bitcoin (BTC) and Ethereum (ETH), that can be traded directly. This now means that users can trade five cryptocurrencies directly on the platform.

Notably, however, XRP, one of the largest cryptocurrencies by market cap, is still missing from the list of available coins.

In its official press release, Schwab's head of digital assets, Joe Vietri, underlined the brokerage's commitment to further expanding its crypto trading options.

Although XRP is not offered directly on the Schwab Crypto trading platform, it is still available to Schwab users in one way or another.

Charles Schwab offers standard and micro futures contracts on XRP through its thinkorswim platform.

In July 2025, the company pointed out the availability of XRP futures with the ticker /XRP and also smaller micro contracts with the ticker /MXP.

It further expanded its derivatives trading platform with the addition of almost 24/7 trading for certain crypto futures, including Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana and XRP, in June 2026.

Charles Schwab's aggressive approach to the crypto industry has been noticeable throughout 2026.

First, the company officially announced Schwab Crypto on April 16. In this announcement, it outlined its plans to introduce direct trading of Bitcoin and Ethereum for retail users.

The next major development came on Oct. 15, when Rick Wurster, the CEO of Charles Schwab, confirmed the introduction of crypto transfers.

The platform now allows eligible customers to transfer eligible crypto assets to and from external wallets through the Schwab Crypto platform. However, this is not yet available to all customers. Access is being rolled out gradually.
